## Why visit

A worthwhile railway-and-beer experience with platform-side seating at the East Lancashire Railway. The appeal is strongest if you enjoy the station setting or can combine the pub with an actual operating day on the heritage railway. It is still a viable pub stop without a train ride, but November railway schedules must be checked separately. Treat older claims about very large beer and cider ranges cautiously: the local CAMRA record itself notes reduced cask availability, and the branch’s cider update conflicts with its real-cider badge. Choose it for ale and setting, with realistic expectations.

## Beer

CAMRA’s detailed update says the cask offer has reduced to around six at most, despite older ten/twelve-pump wording.

## Cider and perry

**Cider reported; qualification needs checking.** Main pub page still shows real cider, but the branch’s April 2026 update explicitly says none then available. Reconfirm; do not use as a dependable cider destination.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Food

Some meal/pizza service is listed, with restricted days. Verify the current menu and kitchen before relying on it.

## Plan the visit

Pub opening and heritage-train operation are separate. CAMRA currently lists Monday/Tuesday closure.

**Getting there:** Near Bury tram/bus interchange; the pub is at Bury Bolton Street heritage station.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
